title: Dominic and the Confession
premise: When the coffin of Aldous Vane, founder of the river town of Marrow's Bend, is found empty during a routine cemetery relocation, night-shift taxi dispatcher Yara Eastwick realizes the last fare logged to Vane's address—thirty years ago, on the night he supposedly died—was dispatched by Yara's own missing father. Pulling the company's rotting paper ledgers, Yara uncovers a pattern of erased rides, hushed confessions, and a cab that never officially existed. As the town's founding families close ranks ahead of the annual Founder's Dinner, Yara discovers Vane faked his death to escape blackmail by his own heirs, and that his father drove him out of town—and paid with his life for what he saw. In the end, Yara finds the living Vane hiding in plain sight as the cemetery's groundskeeper, forces a public confession at the anniversary dinner, and chooses truth over the loyalty that kept the town silent for three decades.
about_author: Silas Sandoval is a former small-town radio operator who spent a decade collecting the strange calls that come in after midnight. He writes mysteries about ordinary people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Yara's POV. During a cemetery relocation, workers open Aldous Vane's coffin and find it empty; Yara, present only because his taxi company handles the funeral traffic, recognizes the grave from an old dispatch log. The beat is quiet dread—the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Night Frequencies
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Unable to let it go, Yara searches the dispatcher office's paper archives and finds his father's handwriting on the last ride logged to Vane's estate, dated the night of Vane's death. His father vanished weeks later. Emotional beat: grief rekindled into obsession.

chapters.title: The Founder's Table
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At a pre-dinner reception, Yara probes the Vane heirs—charitable son Marcus, brittle widow-figure Camille—and notices they already knew about the exhumation before it was public. Beat: first taste of how power smooths over questions.

chapters.title: Fare Unknown
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A retired driver, Odette, admits the 'ghost cab'—an unregistered car used for off-book runs by the founding families—and warns Yara that two people who asked about it died conveniently. Beat: loyalty vs. truth crystallizes; Odette chooses silence.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Following the ghost cab's old route along the river, Yara finds his father's missing dispatch badge wedged in a boathouse owned by Marcus Vane. Someone watches him leave. Beat: fear arrives—he is no longer invisible.

chapters.title: The Groundskeeper
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara confronts the cemetery's reclusive groundskeeper, whose hands and voice don't match his story, and finds a thirty-year-old photograph of Vane alive. The man denies everything—but leaves Yara's gate unlocked. Beat: hope tangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Camille's Ledger
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Camille, drunk and frightened, shows Yara the family ledger: Vane discovered his heirs were laundering money through the town itself, so he staged his death to gather proof. She begs Yara to stop before the dinner. Beat: sympathy for the corrupt; the theme sharpens.

chapters.title: Anniversary Eve
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the eve of the dinner, Yara's apartment is searched and Odette is hospitalized after a 'fall.' Marcus offers Yara his father's case file—if Yara drops everything. Beat: the corruption of power offered as a bargain; Yara refuses.

chapters.title: A Glass Raised
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, climax at the Founder's Dinner. Yara hijacks the toast with the ledger, the badge, and the groundskeeper—who walks in and confesses: he is Aldous Vane, and Yara's father died helping him hide the evidence. Marcus is arrested mid-toast. Beat: catharsis at cost.

chapters.title: Last Call
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, resolution. Weeks later, Vane testifies, the town reckons with its founding myth, and Yara learns his father's final dispatch was a message meant for him. He takes the day shift—or doesn't—but finally speaks at his father's memorial. Beat: memory honored, truth survived.
